chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Ballrooms of the forties and the three bands
summary: Few Latin bands were as versatile; Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez later joined him at the Palladium.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I see. Okay. You had a lot of ballrooms to work in then, in the forties, right? You had, you worked the Savoy Ballroom, you worked the jazz clubs and then you were working the Latin clubs. You worked in the Park Palace and the Alma Dance Studios, which later became the Palladium Ballroom.
Was there any other bands, Latin-American bands, working at all these places the same as you?
No, there wasn't many bands, as a matter of fact, there was .....
Was there any other band as versatile as the Machito band in '47, '48 or '49?
No, no. When the thing started to flourish for the new bands was Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez, so we three played there at the Palladium.
